entities.summary: Arculf was a Frankish churchman who toured the Holy Land around 670. Bede claimed he was a bishop from Gaul. According to Bede's Ecclesiastical History of the English People, Arculf was shipwrecked on the shore of Iona on his return from his pilgrimage. He was hospitably received by Adomnán, the abbot of the island monastery from 679 to 704, to whom he gave a detailed narrative of his travels. Adomnán, with aid from some further sources, was able to produce De Locis Sanctis, a descriptive work in three books dealing with Jerusalem, Bethlehem, other sites in the Holy Land, and briefly with Alexandria and Constantinople.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Arculf's pilgrimage and subsequent account to Adomnán helped shape our understanding of the Holy Land during the early medieval period. His narrative likely influenced De Locis Sanctis, a significant descriptive work that provided valuable information about Jerusalem and other sites in the region.
